voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: In February 2013, a 21-year-old student named Elisa Lam stepped into an elevator at the Cecil Hotel in Los Angeles.
The doors did not close. For ninety seconds, she pressed buttons, stepped into the hallway, stepped back in. The security camera recorded what it recorded.
She was not seen alive again.
Two weeks later, guests complained the water tasted wrong. The autopsy found her in the rooftop tank.
The lid was heavy. There was no sign of anyone else. The coroner ruled it accidental.
